clue.text: This wheel from a bicycle gives space pilot initially his motive power

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the words space and pilot

parts.note: a space pilot is driven by a rocket, his source of motive power

explanation.surface: A bicycle part is said to give an astronaut his propulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'space pilot', S and P; 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel engaging the chain is the cog on a bicycle's pedal or hub.

clue.text: Nameless FBI type supports its return as a mark of disgrace

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits below the other
return asks for the word its to be read backwards
N is short for name, so nameless means that letter is dropped

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent

explanation.surface: An anonymous federal agent backs a comeback that brings shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ITS into STI; 'Nameless' drops N from GMAN to leave GMA, which 'supports' it by sitting below.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a stain on one's reputation, a brand of shame.

clue.text: Communist and German worker surplus to requirements

parts.note: Red is a familiar label for a Communist
und is the German word for and
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A Communist and a German labourer are no longer needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant describes something superfluous, or a worker laid off.

clue.text: Travelled effortlessly with Edward following the shore-line

indicators.note: following puts the Edward piece after the other

parts.note: the coast is the shoreline
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone cruised along with a friend, tracing the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move freely without power or effort, as a cyclist freewheeling.

clue.text: Proverbially human failing, this bloomer

definitions.meaning: the proverb says to err is human
a bloomer is British slang for a blunder

explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is the failing the proverb calls human, and a bloomer is a blunder.

clue.text: A swan, we note, was one of Titania's attendants

parts.note: a cob is a male swan
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A swan is claimed to have served the fairy queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; her fairies include Peaseblossom, Moth, Mustardseed and this one.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play, one of the fairies waiting on the queen bears the name of a spider's tangled thread.

clue.text: Turn up in wood with eastern delicacy

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the word for wood

parts.note: oak is a wood

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act

explanation.surface: Someone appears in a forest carrying an oriental treat.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a stage act; 'up' reverses ACT to TCA, which goes 'in' OAK, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish oat biscuit is offered here, a little generously, as a treat to eat.

clue.text: Silence for Mrs Battle's diversion

definitions.meaning: ...! is an old call for hush
Charles Lamb's essay Mrs Battle's Opinions on ... describes a lady devoted to the card game

explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation demanding quiet is also the card game that Lamb's Sarah Battle loved.

clue.text: Subject to heat and light, say, to make plastic

parts.note: to bake is to subject to heat

indicators.note: say signals the word light spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: the word light, said, can be spelt lite

explanation.surface: Instructions for making plastic with an oven and lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives LITE, the commercial spelling that sounds like 'light'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakelite was an early synthetic resin, the material of old telephones.

clue.text: There's room on the island for the astronaut

parts.note: room means space
the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: There is space to spare on an island for a space traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman is a space traveller, one who flies beyond the atmosphere.

clue.text: Mysteriously oriental disproof of "What goes up must come down"

definitions.text: Mysteriously oriental disproof of "What goes up must come down"

parts.words: Mysteriously oriental disproof of "What goes up must come down"
parts.note: a fabled conjuring feat from the subcontinent in which a coil of cord rises skyward and stays up, defying gravity

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary illusion has a cord climbing upward unsupported, seeming to refute the law of gravity.

clue.text: Alice, a fabulous one, the Unicorn thought

definitions.text: Alice, a fabulous one, the Unicorn thought

parts.words: Alice, a fabulous one, the Unicorn thought
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass the Unicorn, meeting Alice, takes her for a mythical creature of fable

explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's Unicorn calls Alice a 'fabulous' beast, the kind of mythical creature he himself is to her.

clue.text: Thing that's a sort of latchet

indicators.note: a sort of latchet is a rearranged form of that word's letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes an object as resembling a shoe fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges LATCHET (an old word for a shoe-thong); 'that's a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal property, an article or possession.

clue.text: Tincture of opium, alum and uranium possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A recipe seems to list a mixture of opium, alum and uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ALUM, AND and U together.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum was the Victorian painkiller made by dissolving opium in alcohol.

clue.text: Familiar form of address — in prison?

definitions.text: Familiar form of address — in prison?

parts.words: Familiar form of address — in prison?
parts.note: an informal name, read whimsically as the name you'd go by in the nick, British slang for jail

explanation.definitionFit: An informal name for someone; nick is British slang for prison, hence the joke.

clue.text: Make use of a flower? Right

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to use a blossom and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as flow-er, a river: the Exe runs through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring strength or influence to bear is to employ it.

clue.text: Elimination of 90 caught in evasion

indicators.note: caught in means the ninety numeral is held inside the evasion word

parts.note: elusion is evasion
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone escaped being ruled out at ninety.
explanation.walkthrough: '90' looks like an age or a score but is a Roman numeral; 'caught in' is the container signal, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion is the act of shutting out or removing something.

clue.text: Positive sign about a Manx-type aquatic mammal

indicators.note: about means the plus sign goes round the other pieces

parts.note: the plus sign is the positive sign

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word type loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An addition symbol surrounds a tailless creature that swims.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat is the tailless breed from the Isle of Man, so 'Manx' here docks the last letter of the word beside it; 'about' wraps the sign round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed platypus is an egg-laying mammal of Australian rivers.

clue.text: Student to return to house

parts.note: L, for learner, stands for a student driver

indicators.note: return means the first to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student goes back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the first TO into OT. House, or housey-housey, is a British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a numbers game of the bingo family, called house in Britain.

clue.text: Scot riding a farm animal? Quite the opposite for the varsity man

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
riding means on, seated upon
Ian is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman on an ox, or the reverse, is a university man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' swaps rider and mount: not Ian on ox but ox on Ian.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxonian is a member or graduate of Oxford University.

clue.text: Catch game for four

definitions.meaning: a form of bridge played by two pairs of partners

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb for picking up a disease and the name of the bridge variant played by four people.

clue.text: First sign a merry wife shows of violent behaviour

parts.note: Aries the ram is the first sign of the zodiac
Mrs Page is one of Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A jolly wife first shows signs of turning violent.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a rampage means a spree of wild destruction.

clue.text: The heart or, say, the rank of Gilbert the Filbert?

indicators.note: say signals the rank's name heard, not written

parts.words: the rank of Gilbert the Filbert
parts.note: the music-hall song calls Gilbert the Filbert the Colonel of the Knuts

explanation.surface: Asking about the essence, or the rank, of a music-hall dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert the Filbert was a 1914 music-hall song about a dandy, 'the Knut with a K'; a filbert being a nut, his rank 'colonel' sounds like the nut's inner part.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of a nut is its innermost part, so figuratively the heart of a matter.

clue.text: Big blow for Conrad

definitions.meaning: Joseph Conrad wrote a novella with this title

explanation.definitionFit: A tropical cyclone is a huge wind, and Joseph Conrad titled an 1902 sea story after one.

clue.text: Danger of a siege in Arthur's time

definitions.text: of a siege in Arthur's time
definitions.meaning: the Siege Perilous was the fatal seat at King Arthur's Round Table, so the siege is one of this

explanation.definitionFit: Peril is grave danger, and the Round Table's forbidden seat was the Siege Perilous.

clue.text: To calculate, put income in two parts

indicators.note: split into two parts, the word income reads in come: put goes inside come

parts.note: the word income, divided, gives in plus come

explanation.surface: An accountant is told to split earnings into two figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'income' must be read as two words, 'in come', which turns the clue into an instruction: one word goes inside the other, splitting it in two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To compute is to work out a figure by arithmetic.

clue.text: Chapter includes this rule of musical composition

definitions.meaning: a cathedral chapter is made up of its clergy members
a rule, and also a piece in which voices imitate one another in turn

explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral chapter's clergy member, a rule or law, and a round-like piece all share one name.

clue.text: Odd sort of animal a terrapin — roundhead type

indicators.note: an odd sort of animal is a strange rearrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A terrapin is called a strange sort of creature, then a Cromwellian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd sort of' rearranges ANIMAL A TERRAPIN. Roundheads were Parliament's supporters in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Parliament against the king in the Civil War was nicknamed a Roundhead for his cropped hair.

clue.text: Like a William of old, following — the golden rule

definitions.meaning: William the ..., Prince of Orange, led the Dutch revolt in the 16th century
the saying is that silence is golden

explanation.definitionFit: William of Orange bore the epithet 'the Silent', and the proverb says holding one's tongue is golden.

clue.text: Confine Scarface inside

parts.note: to intern is to confine, as in wartime
Scarface was the nickname of the gangster Al Capone

explanation.surface: A gangster is to be locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal means on the inside rather than outside.
